findings: The current official tree supports one ordinary 180-credit pathway: 60 first year; 48 required, 6 restricted and 6 free in year two; 6 required, 6 restricted, 36 free and 12 thesis in year three. General introduction prose calls year-two choice twelve credits, which is consistent with restricted six plus genuinely free six. No invented extra component or double-counted philosophy/placement.

Focus on Women and Arts Education retain the existing neutral nonrepeated six-credit choices. Dance Developments twelve credits is not cut in half. First-year certificate versus positive BSA versus recommended prior history remain distinct. From Text to Performance requires positive Theatre BSA and Dramaturgy passed; the thesis requires the first year and all compulsory second-year courses. Normal earlier completion satisfies these gates.

Diagnostic language test and tutoring are zero-credit obligations. Free study remains forty-two credits with university-level, Board approval, introductory twelve-or-specified-twenty-four and nonduplication rules. A minor, foreign study and internship are options, not compulsory. The published internship example has twelve credits and at least336hours including a report. Current transition replaces older compulsory placement/current-discourse titles rather than stacking them.

The defining external work is academic theatre inquiry, not merely actor training: four recurring theory/history/analysis/dramaturgy lines, weekly live-performance visits, historical source work, theatre-text analysis, dramaturgical research and collaborative theatrical making. The thesis uses supervised independent scientific inquiry and critical analysis with identifiable original contribution, not necessarily new experimental data.

All58 exact interests are reconciled:12 generator rows owned once across the three tested purposes;30 support topics,6 illustrations and10 conditional outcomes. Optional dance/musical study is not falsely mandatory. Career and further-study possibilities are not guarantees.

The strongest UCR responses are real: literary drama and Greek tragedy; creative poetic voice, embodiment and independent artistic practice; cinematic acting, mise-en-scene and spectatorship; Media & Race explicitly includes theatre among historical media alongside archival work; Indigenous and gender arts-based history; qualitative archives/interviews; museum criticism; actual school-based rhetorical education and public heritage projects. These counterexamples require narrowing the older blanket claims that UCR lacked performance, archives or education.

Three whole current feasible24-course programmes test those combinations with literary/historical, performance/media, and cultural/social priorities. The completed objects remain literature/media or broader cultural-social inquiry without sustained theatre-history, dramaturgy and live-production analysis. This is a programme-level subject/method judgment, not an exact-equivalence quota, degree-title, language, actor-training or professional-licence rule. Availability failures in initial palettes were repaired, not used to infer no-match.

All151 active identities were screened and45 plausible contributions read; description-only courses receive full supported consideration and excluded Walcheren material is not used. Final trials meet formal earlier prerequisites, offerings, four per term, first-year PPD and advanced-course rules, with sensible introductory progression. No accepted UCR programme, optional research or forced alignment remains.
